_meta.model: ONE master index for the whole Manage Scripts tree. Flat scripts[] array. Minimal rows: name, folder, state, calls, scriptRef. The renderer builds the folder tree from each row's `folder` and the CALLS/CALLED-BY graph from `calls[]`; `calledBy` is DERIVED at render time by inverting every row's calls[] and is NEVER stored. Listing is not loading: the tree + graph read only this file; a body is fetched lazily on drill-in.
_meta.folderTreeNote: CORRECTED 2026-07-29. schemaVersion 2.0 used imports/navigation/triggers/utilities, which matched nothing in the file; README.md carries the struck claim and why that shape of rot is the dangerous kind. `utilities` survives as ONE flagged divergence holding the shared commitRecord helper - Michael to confirm whether the live file has that folder.
_meta.bodyNature: DICTATION reference (the exact steps to type into Manage Scripts, narrative as native # comment lines) - NOT paste-round-trippable, because FileMaker's script clipboard is XML. Unlike .fmcalc.
_meta.keying: Script names are unique per FileMaker file, so `name` is a safe graph key.
_meta.callsResolution: calls[] may target a script OR a custom function; the linter resolves against this file first, then functions/_index.json.

stateValues.built: Verified present in the file on a named date.
stateValues.superseded: DO NOT IMPLEMENT. Written against an older schema. See supersededWhy.

_meta.stateNote: `state` added 2026-07-29. The ClickUp source pages carried a 2026-06-18 self-audit naming 5 scripts as needing rewrite and 2 as needing review, and six weeks passed with nothing moved - because the finding lived in a status table instead of on the object. Now the warning travels with the thing it warns about.
_meta.capDiscipline: Keep rows minimal so this master index stays under the ~30KB read cap. If it crosses, shard by top-level folder behind a pointer - still no renderer change.
_meta.buildOrderNote: `buildOrder` reflects the v1 build sequence. ORDER IS A CORRECTNESS MATTER, not a preference: on FMP19 there are no native transactions, so atomicity needs every write in a transaction to flow through ONE relationship from ONE parent record. That parent is the ReceivedFunds receipt. Build the txn_* wrapper before the receipt table exists and the only available parent is Loans - so one check across two loans has TWO parents and Revert Record can only roll back half, shipping a silent partial rollback. Table before wrapper.

scripts.name: txn_Begin
scripts.note: Set Error Capture [On], establish the single parent context. NO engine transaction underneath - say so in the comments.

scripts.name: txn_Commit
scripts.note: The ONLY place Commit Records may appear. A stray commit inside a txn block is the usual silent break.

scripts.name: txn_Rollback
scripts.note: Revert Record on the PARENT, discarding the whole uncommitted set. Must fail loudly, never swallow an error to keep a routine moving.

scripts.supersededWhy: Keys off fkProperty instead of the loan-first spine. THE routine the atomicity requirement exists for: oldest interest, then fees, then principal, writing PaymentApplications. A half-applied payment is corrupt money data.
